header:
How diamond prices work:
natural vs lab-grown

lines.text: A 1-carat natural diamond has lost half its value since 2021.
lines.say: A one-carat natural diamond has lost half its value since twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: The average 1-carat stone fell from $8,007 in 2021 to $3,898 in September 2026, per CNBC.
lines.say: The average one-carat stone fell from about eight thousand dollars in twenty twenty-one to about thirty-nine hundred in September twenty twenty-six, according to CNBC.

lines.text: Natural diamonds sell rarity. Big miners like De Beers decide how many rough stones reach the market.
lines.say: Natural diamonds sell rarity. Big miners like De Beers decide how many rough stones reach the market.

lines.text: But after a post-Covid glut, De Beers' average rough price fell 7% in 2025, to $142 a carat.
lines.say: But after a post-Covid glut, De Beers' average rough price fell seven percent in twenty twenty-five, to a hundred forty-two dollars a carat.

lines.text: Then there's lab-grown: real diamonds, same chemistry, made in a factory.
lines.say: Then there's lab-grown: real diamonds, with the same chemistry, made in a factory.

lines.text: Their share of engagement rings jumped from 12% in 2019 to 61% in 2025, per The Knot.
lines.say: Their share of engagement rings jumped from twelve percent in twenty nineteen to sixty-one percent in twenty twenty-five, according to The Knot.

lines.text: Their price follows factory costs, not rarity. Wholesale prices fell roughly 74% since 2020.
lines.say: Their price follows factory costs, not rarity. Wholesale prices fell roughly seventy-four percent since twenty twenty.

lines.text: So natural sells scarcity, lab-grown sells price, and both have gotten cheaper.
lines.say: So natural sells scarcity, lab-grown sells price, and both have gotten cheaper.

post.ig:
A 1-carat natural diamond has lost half its value since 2021.

CNBC (Sept 2026): average 1-carat stone $8,007 in 2021, $3,898 now.
De Beers' average rough price fell 7% to $142 a carat in 2025.
Lab-grown went from 12% of engagement rings in 2019 to 61% in 2025 (The Knot). Their wholesale prices fell about 74% since 2020.
Natural sells rarity. Lab-grown sells price.

Sources: CNBC (Sept 26, 2026), De Beers 2025 results, The Knot, JCK.
